data.gender_notes: Elfatiha is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The first verse of the Quran, which is recited before every prayer and is considered a source of blessings. The name Elfatiha carries the meaning “Opening, Blessing” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Elfatiha usually hope their child will grow to embody opening, blessing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the beginning of a spiritual journey and the opening of the heart to the divine.
data.etymology: Elfatiha belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Opening, Blessing.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Elfatiha total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_urdu.name: الفاتحہ
in_urdu.meaning: قرآن کی پہلی سورة، فتح اور ابتدا
in_urdu.long_meaning: قرآن مجید کی افتتاحی سورة جسے سورة الفاتحہ کہا جاتا ہے، یہ وہ سورة ہے جس کے ساتھ ہم قرآن کی تلاوت شروع کرتے ہیں، اس سورة میں سات آیات ہیں، اور اس میں اللہ تعالیٰ کی حمد و شان کی عظمتوں کا بیان ہے، اور اس میں سیدہ راستے پر چلنے کی درخواست کی گئی ہے

in_english.name: Elfatiha
in_english.meaning: The opening chapter of the Quran, beginning and commencement
in_english.long_meaning: The first chapter of the Holy Quran, known as Surah Al-Fatiha, is the opening surah which Muslims recite to start their reading of the Quran. It consists of seven verses and expresses gratitude and praise to Allah, while requesting guidance and the straight path.

data.cultural_impact: The Elfatihah — also known as Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim — is a verse of the Quran that holds immense cultural and spiritual significance for Muslims around the world. This verse, which translates to "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," is the opening line of the holy book of Islam. Being the first verse, it signifies the importance of starting all affairs, be it reading the Quran or conducting daily prayers, with the remembrance of Allah. Its recitation is a profound reminder for Muslims of the divine purpose and origin of their faith and actions.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the Elfatihah verse is believed to bring numerous blessings and rappour with Allah. It is a deeply personal and solemn act for Muslims to recite this verse, as it signifies the recognition of one's dependence on Allah and submission to His will. Recitation of the Elfatihah is believed to purify the heart and soul, as it is a reminder to always strive towards maintaining a connection with Allah. The Elfatihah is also the first verse of the Quran to be revealed to the Prophet Muhammad, which further adds to its spiritual and revered status in Islam.
